recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if FHIR-I later decides concrete canonical-resource status comments should duplicate the base warning, or if separate external tracking is needed for the Feature Capability IG/subscriptions-framework follow-up.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive with Modification R6 issue asking to clarify that a canonical resource status of active describes the artifact lifecycle, not whether a server supports or enables that artifact for use, and to point server support declarations to CapabilityStatement feature declarations.
initial_application: Upstream commit 0fe79c935e6b847a8f6a6aba969a7588a648e597, "FHIR-47235 Active canonical resources and status fields", changed source/canonicalresource/structuredefinition-CanonicalResource.xml to add the requested support/enabled warning to CanonicalResource.status.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini makes canonicalresource an active interface and maps MetadataResource.status to CanonicalResource.status; ActivityDefinition, PlanDefinition, Questionnaire, and SubscriptionTopic are active resources, but the Jira resolution specifically selected the base CanonicalResource.status comment rather than requiring duplicate comments on each concrete status element. Confluence minutes record the 2024-09-09 FHIR-I persuasive-with-modification vote, and WGM minutes put FHIR-47235 in the Feature Capability IG discussion, matching the non-core CapabilityStatement feature follow-up. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch already contains the requested CanonicalResource.status text, so the reconciliation published an empty no-change audit commit.
